main_text.l: Tenacitas eft, per quam fubftantia mixti fit len-
ta, & tenaciter cohærens.
Illius fcilicet, quod multo humido aqueo, cū
ficco terreo fubtiliore probè permixto, ac lento
calore cocto, eft præditum.
Ratione tenacitatis mixtum aliquando fit tra-
ctile, ut trahendo in partes longas latasq; extendi
posfit: aliquando ductile, ut istu violento in lon-
gum latumq; diduci queat.
Prefsilitas eft, per quam corpus mixtum pref-
sum in feipsum fe arctius colligere potest.
Cujus nempe fubstantia ratione humidi, cum
ficco cocti ac uniti, est porofa.
Idq; vel per impressionem certam quandam
formam recipiendo : vel per condensationem
crafsius fiendo.
Siccitatis autem respectu mixto inest Humecti-
litas: vis admittendi imbibendiq; humorem, in
mixto, quod copioso ficco terreo, porofo, atque
humore destituto, pollet.
Atque hæ qualitates mixti constitu-
tionem respiciunt.
Ad ejusdem dissolutionem pertinent, quæ
vel mixti partium disjunctionem, vel totalem il-
lius destructionem inducendi vim habent.
Prioris generis sunt, tum fractilitas & friabilitas;
tum fectilitas & fissilitas.
Fractilitas est, per quam in majores & inæqua-
les partes mixtum frangi potest.

page.notes: Scan is a 17th-century Latin text; headings "Atque hæ qualitates..." set in italic and treated as level 2 heading. Long s rendered as s; "Tractile" and "Ductile" read as tractile/ductile from italic print, moderately certain. Running head read as "DE QVALITATIBVS MIXTI" (printed in small capitals with the page number 18 at left). The "Vt" at lower right is the catchword for the next page and is recorded in bottom_margin.
